# NYC-Tron UI: full component reference

> Independent, themeable UI library for React Native 0.88 and Expo SDK 58 (iOS, Android and web, plus isolated Windows and macOS adapters). 164 public component exports in 22 groups, each imported from its own package subpath. The consuming app owns theme tokens and state. Packages ship as GitHub Release tarballs, not npm. Stability labels are proposals awaiting owner confirmation; platform statuses are recorded measurements, not device sign-off. Generated by tooling/llms.mjs from docs/library/components.json and the documentation catalog. Do not edit by hand.

Rules for agents writing app code with this library:

- Import every component from its subpath, for example `import { Button } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/Button";`. Never import from a package root barrel such as `@nyc-tron/ui` when a subpath exists.
- Style with the app's semantic tokens (`bg-primary`, `text-text`, `border-border`, `rounded-control`); never hardcode colors. The app defines the variables listed in docs/THEME_TOKENS.md for light and dark.
- Keep app state in Zustand stores and pass it in through props; resources stay in refs.
- Use the library components and React Native primitives; do not write raw HTML UI.
- Keep every accessible name, focus order, text scaling and reduced-motion behavior; follow each component's accessibility notes.
- Report a platform as supported only where the entry says so. "not verified" means no recorded measurement.

Platform policy from the inventory:

- tier1 (ios, android, web): No complete T3 evidence packet is recorded by this inventory; historical receipts are not promoted to candidate acceptance.
- tier2 (macos, windows): D5 measurements retain their original archive, graph and date; absent or conflicting measurements are not verified.
- tier3 (visionos, quest, pico): Not verified for 1.0.0. Physical hardware scenarios, including pen/palm, fold postures, screen-reader speech and multi-display, remain not verified.
- Evidence record desktopD5: docs/desktop-support.json (archive nyc-tron-ui-1.0.0-rc.1.tgz, measured 2026-11-12). A "supported" or "struck" desktop status cites this record.

Each component section lists its import, inventory id, stability proposal, platform statuses, props, a minimal example and accessibility notes. Sections are grouped by import path; package-root barrel exports are listed under the subpath that exports the same declaration.

# NYC-Tron UI guides

> The documentation site guides as plain text: Getting started, Installation, Theming, Platform support, Migration, Changelog, Versioning policy, Contributing, Distribution proposal. Generated by tooling/llms.mjs from docs/library/components.json and the documentation catalog. Do not edit by hand.

## Getting started (getting-started)

Install one component, connect your theme and read the evidence for your target platform.

### Start with your app

NYC-Tron is an independent UI library for React Native and Expo. It ships general app components. Import only the pieces you need. Editor controls such as faders, timelines and color pickers live in Nitro Forge’s @nitro-forge/editor-controls, which builds on Tron.

The current release is v1.0.0-rc.2. The new stable/preview list is a proposal awaiting owner confirmation. A passing install or source check does not certify every component on every platform.

- Installation: the "installation" guide in llms/guides.txt
- Browse components: the component index in llms.txt

### Choose a contract

Each component page names the public import, generated props, example, accessibility notes, proposed stability and measured platforms. Aliases remain visible. Native-only controls retain their host requirements.

## Installation (installation)

Add the published core and UI tarballs to a new or existing Expo app with one install command.

### Create an app

If you already have an Expo app, skip creation and run the install command from its root. Keep the existing runtime, navigation and window contract.

```
npx create-expo-app@5.0.0 my-app --template blank-typescript
cd my-app
```

### Install the release

npm 12 requires --allow-remote=all for remote tarballs; npm 11 ignores the flag. Use npm for these URLs rather than expo install: the tested Expo CLI path rejects remote URLs. The command updates package.json and the npm lockfile.

Core and UI are enough for Button. Some components need optional peers; inspect their import and platform notes before adding them.

```
npm install --allow-remote=all \
  https://github.com/mikevocalz/NYC-Tron-UI/releases/download/v1.0.0-rc.2/nyc-tron-core-1.0.0-rc.2.tgz \
  https://github.com/mikevocalz/NYC-Tron-UI/releases/download/v1.0.0-rc.2/nyc-tron-ui-1.0.0-rc.2.tgz
```

### Render Button

Copy this exact example to App.tsx. It introduces no React state. Fonts stay with your app. Colors, radius and density come from semantic tokens: import the optional default theme or define your own, as the theming guide shows, before treating this as your production styling.

```
import { Button } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/Button";

export default function App() {
  return <Button title="Hello" onPress={() => {}} />;
}
```

### Run your target

A development build is required for native modules that Expo Go does not include. Core UI components do not by themselves prove a native adapter is installed or measured.

If npm reports ERESOLVE, compare the app runtime and optional peer ranges with the support guide. Do not use --legacy-peer-deps to hide a mismatch.

```
npx expo start
# For web, add the Expo-compatible web peers first:
npx expo install react-native-web react-dom
npx expo start --web
```

- Theming: the "theming" guide in llms/guides.txt
- Platform support: the "platform-support" guide in llms/guides.txt

## Theming (theming)

Use the optional default theme and provider, override its tokens, or keep your app’s own tokens in charge.

### How components get their colors

Components never hardcode colors. Every recipe reads semantic tokens such as --color-primary and --color-surface-raised. NYC-Tron ships an optional neutral light and dark default theme and a TronThemeProvider; your app can use them, override any token, or replace them with its own. There is no NYC-MON palette in the library.

### Use the default theme

Resolve @source from the location of your own stylesheet. theme.css declares every token for Uniwind’s light and dark variants, so Tailwind generates the utilities the components use. Redefine a token after the import to change it. Import the file from CSS; a JavaScript import resolves to the presets module.

```
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "uniwind";
@import "@nyc-tron/core/theme.css";
@source "../node_modules/@nyc-tron/ui/dist/components";
```

### Wrap the app in TronThemeProvider

Without a theme prop the provider uses tronLightTheme or tronDarkTheme; colorScheme is "system" by default and also takes "light" or "dark". createTronTheme deep-merges your overrides into a base theme and validates the result. useTronTheme() returns the nearest provider’s theme, resolved scheme and variables, or null without a provider.

The provider passes the theme to Uniwind’s ScopedVariables (an optional peer). On web it sets the tokens and the @expo/ui web variables on a wrapper element. On iOS and Android Uniwind resolves className utilities below it against the theme; native @expo/ui controls keep platform colors. It has been checked with unit and source tests, not on a device or simulator.

```
import { createTronTheme } from "@nyc-tron/core/theme";
import { tronLightTheme } from "@nyc-tron/core/presets/tron";
import { TronThemeProvider } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/theme/TronThemeProvider";

const brand = createTronTheme(tronLightTheme, { colors: { primary: "#6d28d9" } });

export function Root({ children }) {
  return <TronThemeProvider theme={brand}>{children}</TronThemeProvider>;
}
```

### Or define the tokens yourself

This path needs no provider and no import from the presets. These are the default light values; define light and dark values through your Tailwind/Uniwind runtime, and test every text, focus and control-boundary pair in your own palette. Missing optional tokens can leave a recipe uncolored without a build error.

The default palette passes WCAG 2.1 AA: text pairs at least 4.5:1, border and focus at least 3:1 against both surfaces. The reference border in the older part of the token guide is 1.58:1 and is unsuitable when it is the only visible input boundary.

```
@theme {
  --color-primary: #1f5fd1;
  --color-on-primary: #ffffff;
  --color-surface-raised: #ffffff;
  --color-surface-sunken: #f1f3f6;
  --color-border: #7a8799;
  --color-text: #15181d;
  --color-text-muted: #5a626e;
  --color-danger: #b42318;
  --color-on-danger: #ffffff;
  --color-accent: #1f7a6d;
  --color-info: #1d5fa8;
  --color-success: #1e7a3c;
  --color-focus: #1f5fd1;
  --radius-control: 8px;
  --radius-card: 12px;
}
```

- Full token contract, default values and deprecated aliases: https://github.com/mikevocalz/NYC-Tron-UI/blob/main/docs/THEME_TOKENS.md

## Platform support (platform-support)

Separate component stability from evidence for a runtime, platform and interaction.

### Proposed library tiers

Tier 1: iOS simulator, Android emulator and web. Every confirmed stable component must pass its individual library evidence packet before stable publication.

Tier 2: publish the measured component lists for Spark macOS and React Native Windows. Their host versions remain isolated and below UI’s React Native peer floor. Use the documented scoped override and only the lane’s support list.

Tier 3: visionOS, Quest, PICO and physical-hardware scenarios are not verified for 1.0.0. This includes pen/palm, fold postures, screen-reader speech and multi-display.

### Read a platform badge

Supported means a recorded measurement exists for that named import in the cited lane. Struck means the lane measurement failed it. Not verified means there is insufficient evidence. None of these badges approves a stability proposal.

Historical D5 measurements retain their rc.1 archive, date and graph. They are not fresh rc.3 evidence. Native compilation, source tests, web rendering and screen-reader speech are separate claims.

- Exact runtime lanes and desktop support lists: https://github.com/mikevocalz/NYC-Tron-UI/blob/main/docs/SUPPORT.md

## Migration (migration)

Move between candidates: the editor-control import change, app state and platform contracts.

### From rc.2 to the standalone library candidate

Breaking: the owner moved the editor controls to Nitro Forge (decision D10, 2026-11-28). Replace each @nyc-tron/ui/components/forge/<path> import with @nitro-forge/editor-controls/<path>. The three precision helpers stayed in Tron: components/forge/inputs/precision, precision-scrubber-model and PrecisionScrubber are now components/shell/precision, precision-scrubber-model and PrecisionScrubber. docs/library/editor-controls-migration.json lists every removed subpath with its replacement. Every other public import path is unchanged.

Compare generated API snapshots, manifests and release checksum files before upgrading. Install the exact candidate’s core and UI archives together. Keep desktop adapter archives from their independently tested lanes.

Your app’s Zustand stores, imperative refs, authored navigation shell, window dimensions and XR scene geometry remain yours. An upgrade is not permission to change them.

### Deprecations

Existing theme aliases remain accepted. A deprecation must name its replacement and migration path before removal. Stable API removal or type changes require a major release and an owner decision. Preview changes must be labelled in release notes.

## Changelog (changelog)

Release history and the work proposed for the next candidate.

### Unreleased: standalone library v1 work

Recorded independent library scope; generated per-export inventory and proposed stability labels; adopted the downstream component program in Forge draft changes.

Breaking (D10): removed the 453 components/forge subpaths. The editor controls are now @nitro-forge/editor-controls in Nitro Forge; the precision helpers moved to components/shell. Added 20 general subpaths the controls build on. See the migration guide.

This documentation site and kitchen-sink work are proposed. rc.3 has not been published by this slice, and the owner distribution review remains pending. No acceptance value or public API is promoted by these docs.

### v1.0.0-rc.2

Published as sixteen GitHub Release tarballs with SHA256SUMS. The install path and candidate-specific evidence are recorded in the release and support documents.

- Exact rc.2 release: https://github.com/mikevocalz/NYC-Tron-UI/releases/tag/v1.0.0-rc.2

## Versioning policy (versioning)

Define the public contract before making a stability promise.

### Stable components

A confirmed stable API is covered by Semantic Versioning: compatible fixes are patches; compatible additions are minors; removals, renames, incompatible types or behavior require a major. Broader support claims require their own evidence.

Stable labels are not yet confirmed in the current proposed manifest. A label alone cannot satisfy release evidence.

### Preview components

Preview is an explicitly experimental API outside the stable component promise. It may change in a minor only when clearly labelled preview in the manifest, docs and changelog. Announce the old and new contract with a migration example.

Preview does not mean inaccessible, undocumented or safe to claim on unmeasured platforms. Preserve compatibility where practical and document all changes.

### Deprecation and distribution

Announce deprecation before removal, retain the old import where compatible and explain migration. Package versions remain synchronized across release archives. The owner approves any public export removal, rename or type change.

- Semantic Versioning 2.0.0: https://semver.org/

## Contributing (contributing)

Add a component, its documentation and evidence in one reviewable change.

### Extend the existing owner

Read AGENTS.md, the public API snapshots and existing component before adding another abstraction. Reusable UI belongs in NYC-Tron; document engines remain in their owning applications. Never import @nitro-forge into Tron.

Use Zustand for component/app state and refs for resources. Keep app-owned semantic tokens and existing platform/window contracts.

### Update the inventory and docs

Add or update the independent package subpath, declarations, meaningful tests, component example and accessibility notes. Regenerate snapshots only while reviewing the API diff. Every public symbol must be classified; a new component must enter the manifest and docs.

Propose a stability label with a reason; the owner confirms it. A stable target needs unit/model, rendered web, installed-tarball iOS/Android, static accessibility and documentation evidence. Do not mark an unrun check passed.

```
pnpm build
node tooling/api-surface.mjs
node tooling/api-signatures.mjs
node tooling/library-components.mjs --write
npm --prefix website ci
npm --prefix website run build
npm --prefix website test
```

### Review

Open a draft PR with skill outputs, actual command/CI evidence and independent reviewer findings. Preserve licenses and dated proof. Do not merge or mark ready on the owner’s behalf.

## Distribution proposal (distribution)

Keep GitHub Release tarballs for 1.0.0 while the owner considers npm separately.

### Recommendation

Retain GitHub Release tarballs for 1.0.0. All sixteen distributable packages are private, and current gates enforce that contract. npm distribution is an owner decision; this proposal publishes nothing.

### What npm would require

Confirm scope/package availability and publishing access; complete licensing and source-availability review; settle peer-range policy and supported runtime claims.

Coordinate private flags, package versions, dist-tags, provenance, release automation and rollback across sixteen packages. Preserve the exact independently tested desktop archives. Add clean npm consumers for each supported lane before claiming the path works.

Only the owner’s exact version/checksum GitHub comment satisfies stable distribution approval. These docs do not alter that record.

## ListItem (@nyc-tron/ui/components/List)

import { createPageWindowHost } from "@nyc-tron/core/window-chrome";
import { WindowTitleBar, useWindowChrome } from "@nyc-tron/ui/components/window/WindowTitleBar";

// In-page geometry only; this does not resize the app's system window.
export default function Example() {
  const host = React.useRef<ReturnType<typeof createPageWindowHost> | null>(null);
  if (!host.current) {
    host.current = createPageWindowHost();
    host.current.open({id:"example",displayId:"page",rect:{x:0,y:0,width:640,height:480}});
  }
  const chrome = useWindowChrome(host.current,"example");
  return <WindowTitleBar chrome={chrome} title="Example document" controls={{kind:"drawn",layout:"windows"}} />;
}

- Id: `@nyc-tron/windows-fluent-fabric/drag-drop#WindowsDragSource`
- Package: `@nyc-tron/windows-fluent-fabric`; category: general components
- Stability: proposed preview; owner confirmation pending, no label approved

- `payload: unknown` (required)
- `scopeId: string` (required)
- `style?: any`
- `windowId: string` (required)

```tsx
import * as React from "react";
import { AppRegistry, Text } from "react-native";
import { useStore } from "zustand";
import { createStore } from "zustand/vanilla";
import { createWindowRegistry } from "@nyc-tron/core/window-lifecycle";
import { createWindowsWindowHost, type WindowsWindowHost } from "@nyc-tron/windows-fluent-fabric/windows";
import { WindowsDragSource } from "@nyc-tron/windows-fluent-fabric/drag-drop";

const model = createStore(() => ({registry:createWindowRegistry(),ready:false,error:""}));
// Requires a real RNW 0.85 Fabric host with the desktop native module.
export default function Example() {
  const host = React.useRef<WindowsWindowHost | null>(null);
  const ready = useStore(model,s=>s.ready);
  const error = useStore(model,s=>s.error);
  React.useEffect(() => {
    let live = true;
    void createWindowsWindowHost({primaryWindowId:"main",componentName:"TronDocsExample",
      owner:{getState:()=>model.getState().registry,commit:registry=>model.setState({registry})},
      onCloseRequested:request=>{void host.current?.resolveClose(request,false)}
    }).then(value=>{if(!live){void value.dispose();return}host.current=value;model.setState({ready:true})}).catch(error=>model.setState({error:String(error)}));
    return () => {live=false;void host.current?.dispose();host.current=null;};
  },[]);
  if (!ready || !host.current) return <Text>{error || "Connecting to the native host…"}</Text>;
  return <WindowsDragSource host={host.current} windowId="main" scopeId="example-document" label="Example drag source" payload={{id:"document-1"}} onCompleted={result=>console.log(result.effect)} />;
}
AppRegistry.registerComponent("TronDocsExample",()=>Example);
```

- Provide a meaningful accessible name for interactive content. Preserve focus order, text scaling and reduced-motion preferences.

export default function Example() {

  if (!binding.current) {
    binding.current = createWindowsNavigationBinding();
    binding.current.transport.setDestinations([{id:"overview",label:"Overview"}], []);
    binding.current.transport.setSelectedId("overview");
  }

}
